headline: UN experts say US strikes in Iran may be war crimes
summary: A UN fact-finding mission says there are reasonable grounds to believe the US committed war crimes in two February strikes in Iran. One hit a school in Minab, killing at least 156 people, 120 of them children, local officials say. The other hit a sports complex in Lamerd. The US says it is investigating Minab and denies hitting Lamerd.

cover_question.q: Are there rules in a war?

cover_answer: Yes. UN experts say the US broke them twice in Iran.
table_question: Does saying it was a mistake make it okay?

5-7.script: In a war far away, a missile hit a school in Iran and many children died. Some experts who work for the United Nations say the American military fired it and broke the rules of war. Even wars have rules, like a game with a referee. You are safe here, and the grown-ups are working out what happened.
5-7.why: If it comes up, the rules-of-war idea gives a small child something to hold.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Wars have rules. One is that you check a target is military before you hit it. Three UN experts say the US didn't in two February strikes in Iran: a school and a sports complex. The US denies one and is investigating the other. The report is a referee's review, not the final call.
8-12.why: Rule, break, review is a chain they know from sports.

13-17.script: Who decides when a country has broken the rules of war? Three UN experts say there are reasonable grounds to believe the US did in Iran, in a school strike local officials say killed 120 children. The US has not answered the report. Who checks the checkers?
13-17.why: Teens can hold two wrongs at once without picking a side first.

5-7.q: Did our country do something bad?
5-7.a: Some experts say the US broke the rules of war. The US says it is still looking into it. That is what the grown-ups are sorting out.

8-12.q: Are there rules in a war?
8-12.a: Yes. One is that you check a target is military before you hit it. The UN experts say the US didn't.
Nothing automatic. The report goes to the UN Human Rights Council. The US has not responded to it.

13-17.a: No. Their words are 'reasonable grounds to believe.' They asked the US for information and got no reply.

13-17.q: Why is Iran's crackdown in the same report?
13-17.a: The mission covers Iran as a whole. It says security forces killed protesters on a staggering scale.

caption:
Yes. UN experts say the US broke them twice in Iran.

A UN fact-finding mission says there are reasonable grounds to believe the US committed war crimes in two February strikes in Iran. One hit a school in Minab, killing at least 156 people, 120 of them children, local officials say. The other hit a sports complex in Lamerd. The US says it is investigating Minab and denies hitting Lamerd.
